title: In-place recovery cannot reach the contract's recovery endpoint
summary: In-place production and staging recovery reuse DR steps 3–6, whose module hook endpoint permits only the off-site recovery executor.
impact: Correctly isolated production/staging executors cannot run their authorized data restoration and staging reset.
recommendation: Define the executor owning the recovery attempt and admit that environment's authorized production, staging or replacement-capacity executor to the internal recovery endpoint, with consistent custody and epoch rules.

title: Recovery-hook contract is scheduled after an earlier mandatory consumer
summary: The shared recovery contract is due at the first AD-12 drill, but earlier staging attempts already require recovery points and in-place resets.
impact: Teams can reach a mandatory staging reset before agreeing the cut, restore and result protocol, blocking further candidates or producing incompatible early implementations.
recommendation: Gate the recovery-point subset before the first staging recovery point and the complete hook/restore contract before the first staging reset or in-place production recovery; first staging deployment is a conservative single gate.

title: Dapr resources can change without activating the change in existing sidecars
summary: HotReload is disabled but consumer restart is specified only for changed Components, leaving other Dapr resource updates without a required activation mechanism.
impact: Sidecars can retain old authorization, subscriptions or HTTP endpoint configuration while release records and rendered objects describe the new state.
recommendation: Require changed effective Dapr resource content or bindings to restart every affected consuming sidecar within the owning application/environment attempt before readiness or qualification passes; qualify policy-only and HTTPEndpoint-only updates.
